Physically based CRT shader for Windows

A virtual CRT tube for any window.

Phoxium captures the window of a game or a program, runs the picture through a physically modelled CRT tube on the GPU and shows the result in its own window, which can go fullscreen over the game.

Download for Windows Source on GitHub
  • Open source MIT
  • Rust · Vulkan · GLSL · Dear ImGui
  • No injection, no install
  • Linear light, floating point

Download

One zip, one executable, nothing to install.

The latest release is read live from GitHub. Unzip it into a folder you own, start your game, then double-click phoxium.exe: no command line is needed.

Each release gives the hash in its notes and in the attached .sha256 file.

Verify the download

# PowerShell
(Get-FileHash .\phoxium-vX.Y.Z-windows-x64.zip -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
# cmd
certutil -hashfile phoxium-vX.Y.Z-windows-x64.zip SHA256

The value must be identical to the one above (upper or lower case does not matter).

Reading the latest release from GitHub…

First run

  1. Download the windows-x64.zip and check it against the SHA-256 of the release.
  2. Unzip it into a folder you own. Do not run it from inside the zip.
  3. Start the game or program you want to capture.
  4. Double-click phoxium.exe. It lists the windows you can capture: type to search, Up and Down to choose, Enter or a double-click to capture.

F10 settings menu F11 fullscreen / framed window CtrlAltF7 A/B bypass CtrlAltEnd quit

Unsigned binaries. The executables are not code-signed (a personal project without a certificate). Windows SmartScreen may say “Windows protected your PC” on the first run: choose “More info”, then “Run anyway”, only after checking the hash. Antivirus tools may also warn about an unsigned program that captures windows and registers hotkeys.

The hash proves that your copy is the published file; it does not replace trust in the project. The source is public and the executables can be rebuilt from it.

  • Windows 11 x64The tested system. Windows 10 version 2004 or later is expected to work (the capture API needs it) but has not been tested.
  • Vulkan 1.3A GPU and driver with Vulkan 1.3. Measured on an NVIDIA laptop GPU; AMD is untested.
  • No network codeThe program sends nothing anywhere. Everything it keeps is in %APPDATA%\Phoxium\.
  • Below 1.0.0A personal project: a minor version may still change behaviour. Bug reports are welcome in the GitHub issues.

Purpose and philosophy

A model of the tube, not a filter over the picture.

The model is physical, not emulated: each source pixel drives the three electron beams of a virtual tube, and each phosphor element of the mask emits light in proportion to the beam energy it receives. In short, every source RGB pixel becomes real RGB light sources.

  • Source RGB is a drive voltage

    A real CRT does not colour-convert. Source RGB values drive the cathodes directly, and the tube’s own primaries and white point define the colour.

  • Linear light, floating point

    Everything is computed in linear light with floating point (FP16, FP32 where needed), fully on the GPU. The output is SDR.

  • Parameters in physical units

    Mask type is a three-way choice. Every other look parameter is independent and physical: a pitch in millimetres, a bandwidth in megahertz, a decay in milliseconds.

  • Tested against a reference

    The physics also exists as an f64 CPU oracle (the crt-model crate); the GPU stages are tested against it.

What a filter gets wrong

Six of the “ten things the shader must get right”, from the project’s CRT knowledge base.

  1. Order of operations

    The video amplifier acts horizontally on the gamma-encoded voltage, before the gun power law. Blurring in linear light is wrong.

  2. The spot grows with brightness

    Dark lines stay thin and bright lines fatten, so a constant beam width is wrong. Scanlines vanish when the beam is about one line pitch wide.

  3. The mask samples the beam

    Each phosphor element lights in proportion to its own beam at its location. Moiré and colour fringing then come for free.

  4. Host pixels are the bottleneck

    A triad needs at least 3 host pixels. Below that the mask is area-filtered, otherwise a moiré appears that no real tube ever showed.

  5. Halation is a ring, not a blur

    Light trapped in the faceplate returns at a radius of about 1.75 times the glass thickness.

  6. Decay depends on the colour

    Red is near-exponential. Green and blue drop fast, then keep a heavy power-law tail that carries light into the next frame.

What it is not

  • No injectionIt runs beside the captured program: nothing is injected into it and nothing in it is changed.
  • No focus stealingOnce a window is captured, the output never takes the keyboard focus from it, except while the settings menu is open.
  • No GPL code reusedOther shaders are inspiration only. Only permissive licences are bundled.
  • No measured replica of one unitPresets are starting points built from published data. Each value carries a confidence tag:
    SsourcedDderivedKstandardEestimate

Capabilities

Everything the tube does, and what gets the picture to it.

Every parameter is tunable live in the menu. Optional modules are off by default, and off means the picture is exactly the one without them.

Capture

Any window

Choose the window in a searchable list. The integer upscale of the game and the black bars around its picture are detected automatically, and the picture is scaled and centred for you.

Capture

Whole screens

Every monitor is in the list as “Whole screen N”, for games that are not a window of their own. The output is then hidden from screen captures, so it never captures itself.

Capture

Capture cards and cameras

A video device can be the source, read through Media Foundation. No choice of the device’s mode, no audio, no deinterlacing; not yet checked with a real capture card.

Capture

Images and test patterns

A still PNG (Open image), or generated patterns from the command line: flat, ramp, lines, grating, checker, crosshatch, point, window, moving bar, PLUGE, moiré.

Capture

Zero-copy, with a CPU fallback

By default the captured picture stays on the GPU. If the PC cannot do that, Phoxium falls back to a CPU copy by itself. On the reference PC: about 0.2 ms per frame instead of about 3 ms at 2560 × 1440.

Output

Fullscreen or framed

F11 toggles a borderless fullscreen output over the game and a resizable framed window with a remembered rectangle. The game keeps the keyboard.

Output

Click-through

The output can ignore the mouse so clicks reach the game under it (CtrlAltF6). The menu takes the mouse back while it is open.

Output

Global hotkeys

Menu, fullscreen, quit, A/B bypass (toggle or hold), next and previous preset, stats overlay, snapshot. Every key can be changed in the menu, with fallbacks when another program owns a chord.

Source

Per-game profiles

Picture area, scaling multiplier and source settings are saved per program and window class and applied when that window is attached. One profile can be the default.

Source

Lost and found

If the captured window closes, the app waits for a new window of the same program and class (30 s by default), then shows the list again.

Source

A turned tube (TATE)

For vertical arcade games the tube turns a quarter turn: the scanlines become the columns of the picture, and the mask and the curvature turn with it.

Output

GPU choice

One GPU runs the whole chain, capture included: by default the adapter of the monitor the output covers, or the one you set in the menu.

Chain

Native raster

Scanlines are native rows: a game shown at ×3 is brought back to its own pixels first. Pixel aspect ratios (8:7 for NES and SNES, 32:35 for Genesis H40) and several prefilter kernels.

Chain

Video amplifier

A low-pass of the drive voltage, horizontally only, with asymmetric rise and fall, optional peaking and a slew limiter. Bandwidth in MHz against the source’s pixel clock.

Chain

Gun law and white balance

Power, GOG or BT.1886 law, cutoff and drive per gun, and colour sets from real standards: SMPTE-C, EBU, Rec.709, NTSC 1953, NTSC-J and a Trinitron set, with their white points.

Chain

Automatic beam limiting

The frame’s average beam current, low-passed in time, lowers the current of the next frame above a threshold. The raster can also breathe with brightness. Off by default.

Chain

Beam and scanlines

A spot whose width grows with beam current, which shapes the scanlines: dark lines stay thin, bright lines fatten.

Chain

Geometry and convergence

Cylindrical or spherical curvature, overscan, pincushion, trapezoid, rotation, convergence per beam and chromatic aberration fringes.

Chain

Three mask types

Aperture grille, slot mask or delta dot, with the pitch in millimetres and optional damper wires. The exact area mean per host pixel: when your display cannot resolve the mask, it is area-averaged.

Chain

Phosphor

Saturation, and the measured P22 persistence: green and blue keep about 5, 3 and 2 % of a frame’s light in the next three frames at 60 Hz; red leaves no visible trail. Monochrome types too: white P4, green P31, P1 and P39, a Philips yellow blend.

Chain

Faceplate optics

Phosphor diffusion, the halation ring, veiling glare, glow (bloom), vignette, glass tint and room light. Behind one Enable switch, off by default; the glow only moves light.

Chain

Output transform

The mask and the scanlines peak above panel white: the SDR headroom is shown and handled (auto, shoulder, physical, mask depth, clip), with tube-faithful or sRGB-matched colours and a final dither.

Optional

Motion clarity New

On a 120 Hz or faster screen (240 or 300 Hz for a 60 Hz game), a rolling scan lights at each refresh only the band of lines the beam crosses; a strobe inserts black frames. Less motion blur, at the cost of brightness. Built and tested, its look at 240 and 300 Hz not yet judged by hand.

Optional

Composite video

Re-encodes the picture as an NTSC or PAL composite (or S-Video) signal and decodes it again: cross-colour, dot crawl, chroma bleed, notch or comb separation, artifact colours.

Optional

Interlace

A manual field mode: alternate frames as fields, or split a woven 480i frame. Field order and a field lock.

Optional

Signal faults

The faults of a poor analogue signal: hum bars, line jitter and crawl, ghosts, noise and snow, a line-tracking band.

Optional

VHS tape and vertical roll

A soft picture, smeared and lagging colour, a head-switching band, dropouts, and a picture that rolls like a set with a lost vertical hold.

Optional

TV controls and flicker

Sharpness, tint, colour, black level and white level, as the knobs of a set, and a refresh flicker beat.

Optional

Ageing and burn-in

Phosphors lose efficiency, blue fastest, so white turns warm; worn guns and a larger spot. Burn-in keeps a wear map per colour, saved per tube preset between sessions: it deliberately damages the picture.

Optional

Cabinet and bezel

A moulded bezel drawn around the picture by the shader, and the glass reflecting it.

Presets

Your own presets

Save as new, rename, delete, duplicate, export and import. User presets are plain .toml files; the shipped ones are never changed.

Performance

Quality tiers

Exact, standard, fast, low: how much work the model costs, never the look. Standard stays within one FP16 step of exact (measured mean 0.012 %, at most 0.2 % of white).

Performance

Automatic quality drop

On by default: when the GPU frame time stays above the refresh period for 3 seconds, the next lower tier is used, and the window title says so. It climbs back when there is headroom.

Tools

Offline render

One frame of a pattern or a PNG through the same GPU pipeline, with no window: an 8-bit PNG or a float PFM. Every render on this page was made with it.

Tools

Diagnostics

A read-only stats overlay (fps, GPU ms, px per triad), GPU time per stage from Vulkan timestamp queries with --stats, and a CSV log.

Tools

Frame pacing

A frame rate cap, optional tearing, a capture rate above 60 fps on recent Windows 11, and a keep-awake switch for long gamepad sessions.

Tools

Snapshot

CtrlAltF2 saves the picture the CRT drew as a PNG.

How it works

The chain, in the order physics applies it.

A fixed chain of GPU stages. The first ones live in voltage space, the gun turns voltage into beam current, and everything after the screen is linear light. Select a stage to see what it models.

Drive voltage Beam current Linear light Display codes Dashed: optional, skipped while off

  1. Drive voltageslot decode

    Source decode

    Reads the captured frame at the centre of each native pixel, so an integer upscale is undone, and turns the code values into the drive voltage of each gun. The model works on the native raster: scanlines are native rows.

  2. Drive voltageslot targetoptional

    Colour target

    The colours of the device the source came from, before the tube: for example the Game Boy Color’s channel mix, the Mega Drive’s measured colour levels, or the colours a television decodes from the NES’s composite signal. An exact identity while the target is “none”.

  3. Drive voltageslot signaloptional

    Composite video

    An NTSC or PAL composite or S-Video encode, the channel, the luma and chroma separation and the decode, in the voltage domain, as a TV fed by an 8-bit era console would do it. The ratio of the source’s pixel clock to the colour subcarrier makes the artifact colours.

  4. Drive voltageslot amp

    Video amplifier

    A Gaussian low-pass of the drive voltage on a horizontally oversampled line, with an asymmetric rise and fall (the smear trails to the right), optional peaking and a slew limiter. It acts on the gamma-encoded voltage, before the gun: isolated one-pixel vertical lines come out dimmer than horizontal ones, as on a real tube.

  5. Drive voltageslots impair tape tvoptional

    Signal faults, VHS tape, TV controls

    Three optional slots on the drive voltage just before the gun: the faults of a poor analogue signal (hum, jitter, ghost, noise and snow), a VHS tape with a vertical roll, and the set’s own knobs (sharpness, tint, colour, black and white level) with a refresh flicker. Every random number is a fixed hash of the line and the frame, so a frame is impaired the same way twice.

  6. Beam currentslot gun

    Electron gun

    Turns the drive voltage into beam current by the gun law (power, GOG or BT.1886), with a cutoff and a drive per gun, and an optional white retune solved from the tube’s primaries and white point.

  7. Beam currentslot abloptional

    Automatic beam limiting

    The frame’s average beam current, low-passed in time, lowers the beam current of the next frame above a threshold (one frame of latency, measured on the GPU with no readback). It can also make the raster breathe with brightness.

  8. Linear lightslot screen

    Beam and geometry

    The beam lands as a scanline profile vertically and a round spot horizontally, and the spot grows with the beam current. The geometry moves the landing position: faceplate curvature, pincushion, trapezoid, rotation, and the convergence of the three beams.

  9. Linear lightslot screen

    Mask

    The same stage multiplies the beam by the mask, per host pixel: aperture grille, slot mask or delta dot, evaluated as the exact area mean over the pixel. Where the host cannot resolve the mask it is prefiltered, with a blend band between, so nothing aliases and nothing steps.

  10. Linear lightslot wearoptional

    Ageing and burn-in

    Phosphor efficiency loss with the hours of use, and a burn-in wear map per colour that static bright parts of the picture write into. The map is kept between sessions, one file per tube preset.

  11. Linear lightslot scanoptional

    Motion clarity

    On a screen that refreshes several times per source frame, each refresh shows only the band of lines the beam crosses in it (rolling), or the whole frame then black (strobe). The slot sits just before the phosphor, so saturation and persistence act on the gated light. The beam, the mask and the glow are drawn once per source frame and held, so each extra refresh costs a small share of the chain.

  12. Linear lightslot phosphor

    Phosphor

    Saturation per channel, then persistence: the afterglow a phosphor keeps after the beam has passed. The decay is colour dependent and follows real time, so a trail lasts as long at 144 Hz as at 60 Hz.

  13. Linear lightslot opticsoptional

    Faceplate optics

    Light crossing the glass: phosphor-layer diffusion, the halation ring, veiling glare, glow (bloom), vignette, glass tint and ambient reflection, all as energy-conserving redistributions. Off by default.

  14. Display codesstage encode

    Output transform

    From the tube’s linear light to the SDR panel: headroom handling for the light above panel white, the tube’s primaries and white, the encode and a final dither. The menu and the stats overlay are drawn after it, over the finished picture.

See the difference

Real renders, straight from the engine.

Every picture in this section was produced by the app’s own offline command, phoxium render, from one original 320 × 240 pixel-art scene drawn for this page, or from a built-in test pattern. Nothing is retouched: the renders are shown at their output size or as pixel-for-pixel crops, saved as JPEG.

Source Phoxium render

Sony KV-class Trinitron consumer TV. The classic console-on-a-TV look. Aperture grille, cylindrical faceplate; the 0.78 mm pitch is an estimate.

phoxium render --image scene.png --preset kv-trinitron-tv --size 960x720 --out crt.png

At 960 × 720 the host pixels cannot resolve most of these masks, so the engine area-averages them, exactly as it does live. The crops below show the masks themselves.

Under the loupe: three mask types

The same scene rendered at 3840 × 2880, then cropped, never rescaled: each tile shows part of a 600 × 450 crop at its own size, one image pixel per CSS pixel. Open a tile for the whole crop.

Colour targets on the same scene

A colour target shows an emulator picture in the colours of the device it came from. The first four start from a four-grey version of the scene, the picture a Game Boy emulator draws; the last two start from the colour scene. Rendered with the bare parameter defaults at 640 × 480.

Optional modules and phosphor types

One switch each, on the Trinitron TV preset (first row), and three monochrome phosphor types on the bare defaults (second row). 640 × 480.

Test patterns

The engine generates its own patterns, the same ones its automated tests use.

The menu

Every parameter, live, inside the output window.

F10 opens the settings menu. Changes apply to the picture at once and are saved. These are real snapshots of the app’s Dear ImGui interface, from its headless UI tests (window titles in the list are sample data).

Enlarge

Choose a window to captureAt start the output window lists the windows that can be captured, each with its program, size and monitor, the most recently used first. Type to filter, Up and Down to choose, Enter or a double-click to capture. Minimised windows are greyed: they deliver no frames until restored.

The menu lives inside the outputF10 opens it, windowed or fullscreen; it can be moved, resized, collapsed and made translucent. The read-only stats overlay (top right: fps, GPU ms, px per triad) never takes input or focus.

Source: what was detected, and your overridesThe native size and the integer scale found, Change source, Open image and Detach, the capture path (zero-copy or CPU copy), and the picture area: Auto finds the game’s picture inside black bars, four limits tune it by hand, in whole source pixels.

PresetsThe shipped presets first, sorted by name, then a separator, then yours, tagged “user”. Picking one applies it at once; an amber dot means parameters changed since. Revert, Reload, Save as new, and Manage files for rename, duplicate, export and import.

Output and headroomThe headroom readout says how far the brightest elements exceed panel white (mask × scanlines × white × exposure) and which mode handles it. Below, the placement readout: native size, picture, px per source pixel, scanline and triad pitch, and how the mask is evaluated.

Gun and whiteColour sets from real standards and tubes are starting points for the tube’s primaries and white point, which stay editable. Then the gun law, gamma, gain, and the cutoff and drive of each gun.

MaskAperture grille, slot mask or delta dot, the pitch in millimetres, stripe fill, edge softness, damper wires, and the tier that decides how the mask is evaluated on your display. The amber dot marks a value that differs from the preset.

Search every panel“Search parameters” finds parameters in every panel by name, id or group; every word must match. Hover a label for what it does; double-click it to reset it to the preset value.

HotkeysEach action shows its chord, with Change and Default, Quit included (it can be changed, never removed). A chord owned by another program is refused with the reason, and a fallback keeps the menu reachable while its key is changed.

GPU and systemThe adapter in use and why, the adapter for the next start (a restart is needed), and the warnings: here, an output on a monitor that another GPU drives, so frames cross adapters.

Known limits

What is not proven yet.

A personal project, still below 1.0.0, with unsigned binaries. The honest list, from the README:

  • Few real games so far. Checked live mostly with a test source of the repository and a few windows on one PC, not yet with a wide range of real games.
  • One reference PC. Measured on one NVIDIA laptop (RTX A2000, with an Intel GPU beside it) and tried on a second one (RTX 3060 Laptop GPU). AMD GPUs and other PCs are untested.
  • SDR only. No HDR output and no HDR colour.
  • Zero-copy capture is not yet validated with a wide range of games and drivers. The CPU copy is the safe choice, one combo away in the menu.
  • Motion clarity is built and tested headless and in the window loop on a 60 Hz screen with a forced count of refreshes; how it looks at 240 and 300 Hz is not yet judged by hand. It flickers at the source rate, which some people find uncomfortable.
  • Weak GPUs. An Intel UHD 770 reaches about 24 frames per second on the slot-mask TV preset at 1920 × 1200, even at the lowest tier. A smaller output window or a lighter preset is the lever.
  • Exclusive fullscreen cannot be captured as a window: run the game in a window or borderless fullscreen. Protected content is captured black; a minimised window sends no frames.
  • The menu takes the focus while it is open, so some games pause. F10 and F11 are global while Phoxium runs; every key can be changed.
  • Tested, not all looked at. Several newer parts are covered by automated tests but not yet checked by hand; the questions log and the changelog say which.
